With years of experience building high-converting stores and content-driven websites, we help businesses launch, optimize, and scale their online presence.

Whether you're launching your first Shopify store, migrating from another platform, or need a custom WordPress website for your content business, we combine technical expertise with a deep understanding of what drives conversions and growth. We specialize in Shopify development for e-commerce stores that need custom features, performance optimization, and ongoing support. items.question: What Shopify development services do you offer?
items.answer: We offer comprehensive Shopify development services including store setup and configuration, custom theme development, app integration, performance optimization, migration from other platforms, ongoing maintenance and support, and SEO optimization for Shopify stores.

items.question: How long does it take to set up a Shopify store?
items.answer: The timeline depends on the complexity of your requirements. A basic store setup typically takes 1-2 weeks, while a fully customized store with advanced features can take 4-8 weeks. We'll provide a detailed timeline during our initial consultation based on your specific needs.

items.question: Can you migrate my existing store to Shopify?
items.answer: Yes, we specialize in e-commerce migrations. We can migrate your store from Magento, BigCommerce, or other platforms to Shopify. Our migration process includes data transfer, product migration, customer data migration, order history (if applicable), and theme customization to match your brand.

items.question: Do you provide ongoing support after the store is launched?
items.answer: Absolutely. We offer ongoing support and maintenance packages to ensure your store continues to perform optimally. This includes regular updates, security monitoring, performance optimization, bug fixes, and feature additions as your business grows.

items.question: How much does Shopify development cost?
items.answer: Pricing varies based on project scope and requirements. We provide custom quotes tailored to your specific needs rather than fixed packages. During our free consultation, we'll discuss your goals and provide a transparent pricing proposal that delivers maximum ROI for your investment.

items.question: Can you customize Shopify themes?
items.answer: Yes, we specialize in custom Shopify theme development. We can modify existing themes or build completely custom themes from scratch to match your brand identity and business requirements. Our themes are optimized for performance, conversion, and mobile responsiveness.

items.question: Do you help with Shopify SEO?
items.answer: Yes, SEO optimization is a crucial part of our Shopify development services. We optimize on-page elements, implement structured data, improve site speed, ensure mobile-friendliness, and provide content optimization strategies to help your store rank better in search engines.

items.question: What payment gateways can you integrate?
items.answer: We can integrate all major payment gateways supported by Shopify, including Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe, Authorize.net, and many others. We'll help you choose the best payment solution for your business and handle the complete integration.

items.question: Can you build custom Shopify apps?
items.answer: Yes, we develop custom Shopify apps to add unique functionality to your store. Whether you need custom checkout features, inventory management tools, or integrations with third-party services, we can build tailored solutions that meet your specific business needs.

items.question: How do I get started with your Shopify development services?
items.answer: Getting started is easy! Simply contact us through our contact form or schedule a free consultation. We'll discuss your project requirements, answer any questions, and provide a detailed proposal. There's no obligation, and we're here to help you succeed.

items.question: What WordPress development services do you offer?
items.answer: We offer comprehensive WordPress development services for content sites, news platforms, and custom websites. This includes custom theme development, plugin customization, performance optimization, content management setup, migration services, security hardening, and ongoing maintenance and support.

items.question: Do you build e-commerce sites with WordPress?
items.answer: No, we specialize in Shopify for e-commerce stores. WordPress is ideal for content-driven sites like news platforms, blogs, corporate websites, and custom content management systems. For online stores, we recommend Shopify which offers better e-commerce features and reliability.

items.question: How long does it take to develop a WordPress site?
items.answer: The timeline varies based on project complexity. A basic content site typically takes 2-3 weeks, while a fully customized site with advanced features can take 6-10 weeks. We'll provide a detailed timeline during our consultation.

items.question: Can you migrate my existing WordPress site?
items.answer: Yes, we handle WordPress migrations from various hosting providers and can help optimize your site during the migration process. We ensure all content, media, and settings are safely transferred to your new hosting environment.

items.question: Do you provide WordPress hosting and maintenance?
items.answer: While we don't provide hosting directly, we can recommend reliable hosting providers and handle all WordPress maintenance tasks including updates, security monitoring, backups, performance optimization, and technical support.

items.question: How much does WordPress development cost?
items.answer: Pricing depends on your project requirements. We provide custom quotes based on your specific needs rather than fixed packages. During our free consultation, we'll discuss your goals and provide transparent pricing that delivers maximum value.

items.question: Can you customize WordPress themes?
items.answer: Absolutely. We can modify existing WordPress themes or build completely custom themes tailored to your brand. Our themes are optimized for performance, SEO, mobile responsiveness, and user experience.

items.question: Do you help with WordPress security?
items.answer: Yes, security is a top priority. We implement security best practices including SSL certificates, security plugins, regular updates, malware scanning, and secure hosting recommendations to protect your site from threats.

items.question: What types of sites are best for WordPress?
items.answer: WordPress is ideal for content-driven sites including news platforms, blogs, corporate websites, portfolios, membership sites, and custom content management systems. For e-commerce stores, we recommend Shopify for better performance and e-commerce features.

faq.title: SEO questions, answered clearly
faq.subtitle: What to expect before choosing an audit, an implementation scope, or ongoing SEO work.

items.question: How long does SEO take to show results?
items.answer: SEO timelines vary with the site’s starting point, competition, technical constraints, search demand, and the speed of implementation. Some technical improvements can be validated quickly, while meaningful visibility and business outcomes usually develop over several months. We establish a baseline and report progress without inventing a universal deadline.

items.question: Do you guarantee first-place rankings?
items.answer: No. Search rankings are controlled by search engines and influenced by competitors, algorithms, demand, and many factors no agency can guarantee. We commit to evidence-based priorities, careful implementation, transparent measurement, and continuous improvement.

items.question: Which website platforms can CartShift work with?
items.answer: We are strongest where we can inspect and implement changes directly, including Shopify, WordPress, and modern custom websites. We can also audit other platforms, but we confirm technical access and implementation constraints before defining the scope.

items.question: Is local SEO included?
items.answer: Local SEO is included where it matches the business model and agreed package. Work can cover Google Business Profile, categories, services, business information consistency, review strategy, citations, and location or service-area pages.

items.question: Does CartShift write SEO content?
items.answer: We can improve page structure, search intent, briefs, on-page copy, titles, descriptions, internal links, and selected priority pages. Large-scale article or landing-page production is quoted separately so expectations, expertise, and quality controls remain clear.

items.question: What access do you need?
items.answer: Access depends on the scope and may include the website CMS or codebase, Google Search Console, GA4, Tag Manager, Google Business Profile, hosting, and relevant reporting tools. We request the minimum practical access and agree on permissions before work begins.

items.question: Can you work with our existing developer or marketing team?
items.answer: Yes. We can implement directly, collaborate with an internal or external team, or provide clearly documented tickets and acceptance checks. Ownership and handoffs are agreed during discovery so work does not stall between strategy and release.

items.question: What is the difference between an SEO audit and ongoing SEO?
items.answer: An audit establishes the baseline, identifies issues and opportunities, and produces a prioritized roadmap. Ongoing SEO adds a recurring implementation and measurement cycle so the site can respond to new data, competitors, content needs, and business priorities.

items.question: Is there a long-term contract?
items.answer: One-time audit and foundation packages do not create an ongoing commitment. Any recurring SEO Growth engagement, notice period, and minimum term are stated clearly in the proposal before work starts; there is no artificial urgency or hidden renewal.

items.question: How is final SEO pricing calculated?
items.answer: Final pricing reflects website size, platform complexity, number of locations or markets, current technical condition, content volume, analytics maturity, access, implementation responsibility, and the pace of work. The listed prices are starting points, followed by a written scope before approval.

meta_description.title: Add a search-ready meta description
meta_description.description: Search engines and AI answer engines use the description to understand the page and influence click-through rate.
meta_description.action: Write a unique 140-160 character description for the homepage that names the offer, audience, and primary reason to buy.

robots_txt.title: Fix robots.txt crawl rules
robots_txt.description: Invalid robots.txt directives can stop crawlers from discovering important product, category, or asset URLs.
robots_txt.action: Validate /robots.txt, remove unsupported directives, and confirm important pages and assets are not blocked.

color_contrast.title: Improve low-contrast text
color_contrast.description: Low contrast makes important copy and buttons harder to read, especially on mobile and for users with impaired vision.
color_contrast.action: Adjust foreground/background color pairs to meet WCAG AA contrast: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

image_alt.title: Add descriptive alt text to images
image_alt.description: Product and content images without alt text lose accessibility context and reduce image-search clarity.
image_alt.action: Add concise alt text to meaningful images and leave purely decorative images empty with alt="".

button_name.title: Name icon-only buttons
button_name.description: Buttons without accessible names are confusing for screen reader users and automated assistants.
button_name.action: Add visible text or aria-label values to every button, especially cart, menu, search, and carousel controls.

link_name.title: Make links understandable
link_name.description: Generic or empty links make navigation unclear and weaken semantic understanding of the page.
link_name.action: Replace vague link labels with destination-specific text and add aria-labels when an icon is the only visible content.

label.title: Connect labels to form fields
label.description: Unlabeled inputs hurt accessibility and can reduce checkout and newsletter form completion.
label.action: Use visible labels or aria-label/aria-labelledby for each form input, select, and textarea.

server_response_time.title: Reduce server response time
server_response_time.description: Slow server response delays every later loading milestone and makes paid traffic less efficient.
server_response_time.action: Enable page caching, review hosting resources, move heavy plugins/apps off the critical path, and add CDN caching.

largest_contentful_paint.title: Speed up the largest visible element
largest_contentful_paint.description: A slow hero image or main content block delays the moment shoppers feel the page is usable.
largest_contentful_paint.action: Identify the actual LCP element and its loading path before applying preload or image changes.

lighthouse_initial_page_load.title: Improve initial page-load performance
lighthouse_initial_page_load.description: Lighthouse measured slow early loading milestones in the tested lab run.
lighthouse_initial_page_load.action: Identify the actual LCP element and its loading path before applying preload or image changes.

lighthouse_js_execution.title: Reduce JavaScript execution and main-thread work
lighthouse_js_execution.description: Lighthouse measured JavaScript or rendering work that can delay interaction in the tested lab run.
lighthouse_js_execution.action: Use the Lighthouse task breakdown to remove unused theme/app code, defer non-critical third-party tags, and split work before menus, filters, and product actions are usable.

lighthouse_layout_stability.title: Stabilize layout during load
lighthouse_layout_stability.description: Lighthouse measured layout movement above the passing threshold.
lighthouse_layout_stability.action: Reserve dimensions for images, embeds, banners, and sticky bars identified by Lighthouse before they load.

lighthouse_server_response.title: Reduce server response time
lighthouse_server_response.description: Lighthouse measured slow initial server response for the tested page.
lighthouse_server_response.action: Review full-page caching, hosting resources, CDN cache rules, and plugins/apps that run before the first HTML response.

total_blocking_time.title: Reduce JavaScript blocking time
total_blocking_time.description: Heavy JavaScript blocks interaction and makes filters, menus, and add-to-cart actions feel laggy.
total_blocking_time.action: Remove unused scripts, defer third-party tags, split large bundles, and audit apps/plugins loaded on every page.

cumulative_layout_shift.title: Prevent layout shifts
cumulative_layout_shift.description: Unexpected movement can cause misclicks and makes product pages feel unstable.
cumulative_layout_shift.action: Reserve width/height for images, embeds, banners, and sticky bars before they load.

document_title.title: Add a descriptive page title
document_title.description: The page title is one of the strongest signals for search listings and browser tabs.
document_title.action: Add a unique title under 60 characters that includes the store name and main product/category promise.

h1.title: Add one clear H1 heading
h1.description: A clear H1 helps shoppers, search engines, and assistive technologies understand the page topic.
h1.action: Add one visible H1 near the top of the homepage that describes the store or primary collection.

ai_structured_data.title: Add AI-readable structured data
ai_structured_data.description: AI answer engines, search rich results, and shopping surfaces need structured facts to understand products, organization details, breadcrumbs, and FAQs.
ai_structured_data.action: Add valid JSON-LD for Product, Organization, BreadcrumbList, WebSite, and FAQPage where relevant, then validate it with Rich Results and schema validators.

ai_product_schema.title: Add Product schema to sellable pages
ai_product_schema.description: Product schema helps search, shopping, and AI answer surfaces understand price, availability, reviews, images, and product identity.
ai_product_schema.action: Add Product JSON-LD to product templates with name, image, description, SKU, offers, availability, priceCurrency, price, and aggregateRating when reviews exist.

ai_social_metadata.title: Add share and preview metadata
ai_social_metadata.description: Open Graph and Twitter card metadata improve how products and collections are summarized when shared, crawled, or cited by assistant-style surfaces.
ai_social_metadata.action: Add og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url, twitter:card, and product-specific preview metadata to key storefront templates.

ai_content_clarity.title: Make pages easier for AI to summarize
ai_content_clarity.description: Thin or poorly structured content gives search engines and AI answer systems fewer reliable facts to cite about your products, policies, and differentiators.
ai_content_clarity.action: Add clear H2 sections, concise product/category explanations, FAQ blocks, policy summaries, and bullet lists that answer buying questions directly.

script_count.title: Reduce storefront JavaScript
script_count.description: Too many scripts slow down rendering and can delay menus, filters, and add-to-cart interactions.
script_count.action: Audit theme/app scripts, remove unused tags, and defer anything not needed for first render.

lazy_loading.title: Lazy load below-fold images
lazy_loading.description: Images below the first viewport should not compete with critical content for initial bandwidth.
lazy_loading.action: Add loading="lazy" to below-fold images while keeping the hero image eager/preloaded.

html_lang.title: Set the page language
html_lang.description: Language metadata helps screen readers pronounce content correctly and helps search engines classify the page.
html_lang.action: Add the correct lang attribute to the <html> element, such as lang="he" or lang="en".

viewport.title: Add a mobile viewport tag
viewport.description: Without a viewport tag, mobile browsers may render the store at desktop width and create a poor shopping experience.
viewport.action: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> to the document head.

cart_visible.title: Make the cart easy to find
cart_visible.description: A hidden cart creates friction for returning shoppers and makes checkout feel less predictable.
cart_visible.action: Add a persistent cart entry point in the header with a clear icon, accessible label, and item count.

add_to_cart_missing.title: Make the purchase action unmistakable
add_to_cart_missing.description: If shoppers cannot immediately identify how to add an item to cart, product intent leaks before checkout begins.
add_to_cart_missing.action: Use a high-contrast add-to-cart or buy-now button on product cards and product pages, with disabled states reserved only for unavailable variants.

checkout_path_missing.title: Expose a predictable checkout path
checkout_path_missing.description: A clear path from cart to checkout reduces hesitation and prevents dead-end shopping sessions.
checkout_path_missing.action: Ensure cart forms, mini-cart drawers, and checkout buttons use visible labels and link to a real cart or checkout route.

checkout_flow_not_verified.title: Checkout flow not verified
checkout_flow_not_verified.description: Checkout flow quality was not tested in this scan.
checkout_flow_not_verified.action: Run a deeper scan that samples category pages, product pages, add-to-cart behavior, cart UI, and checkout entry points before making checkout recommendations.

payment_cues_missing.title: Show accepted payment methods
payment_cues_missing.description: Payment cues reduce risk perception before shoppers commit to checkout.
payment_cues_missing.action: Add accepted payment logos or wallet labels near the cart, checkout button, and footer.

visual_contrast_audit.title: Fix visible contrast risks
visual_contrast_audit.description: Low contrast makes merchandising, pricing, and checkout copy harder to read on real devices.
visual_contrast_audit.action: Review the captured page against WCAG AA and adjust text, button, and badge colors until normal text reaches 4.5:1 contrast.

mobile_layout_friction.title: Repair mobile shopping friction
mobile_layout_friction.description: Mobile layout issues make browsing, tapping, and checkout slower for the traffic most likely to abandon.
mobile_layout_friction.action: Remove horizontal overflow, resize small tap targets to at least 44px, and retest product cards, menus, cart drawers, and checkout CTAs at 320-390px widths.

checkout_trust.title: Add checkout trust cues
checkout_trust.description: Trust cues near purchase actions reduce hesitation when shoppers are about to enter payment details.
checkout_trust.action: Place secure payment, returns, warranty, or guarantee messaging near cart and checkout entry points.

reviews.title: Show customer reviews or ratings
reviews.description: Social proof helps new shoppers validate quality, sizing, service, and delivery confidence.
reviews.action: Add review snippets, star ratings, testimonials, or UGC near product and collection decision points.

privacy_policy.title: Make privacy policy visible
privacy_policy.description: Visible policies build trust and help shoppers understand how their information is handled.
privacy_policy.action: Link privacy, returns, shipping, and terms pages from the footer and checkout-adjacent areas.

accessibility_audit.title: Run a full accessibility audit
accessibility_audit.description: The fallback analyzer could not gather enough accessibility detail to verify WCAG risks.
accessibility_audit.action: Run a browser-based accessibility audit and fix keyboard, label, alt text, and contrast failures.

mixed_content.title: Remove mixed content from secure pages
mixed_content.description: HTTP assets on an HTTPS storefront can be blocked by browsers, break product media, and weaken shopper trust.
mixed_content.action: Replace every http:// asset, stylesheet, script, image, and canonical storefront link with HTTPS or protocol-relative URLs from trusted hosts.

insecure_form_action.title: Secure every form submission
insecure_form_action.description: Forms that submit to HTTP can expose emails, account details, or checkout handoff data in transit.
insecure_form_action.action: Move newsletter, account, cart, and checkout form actions to HTTPS endpoints and verify redirects never downgrade to HTTP.

measuredFindings.subtitle: Lighthouse lab results for the tested URL. They are reliable for the run, but not field data.

verifiedFixes.subtitle: Items backed by Lighthouse, rendered browser checks, or sampled product pages.
